"""Original Workspace -> explicit editable GIS request; no replacement scientific engine."""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from . import gis_project as gis


def _artifact(workspace, directory, item):
    """Translate the original describe_file contract without altering its identity."""
    path = gis.checked(directory, item)
    result = {"path": path.relative_to(workspace.root).as_posix(),
              "bytes": item["bytes"], "sha256": item["sha256"]}
    return result


def _raster_companions(workspace, item):
    import rasterio
    result = []
    primary = gis.local(workspace.root, item["path"])
    with rasterio.open(primary) as src:
        for filename in src.files:
            p = Path(filename).resolve(strict=True)
            if p == primary:
                continue
            if not p.is_relative_to(workspace.root):
                raise ValueError("Raster companion is outside the retained Workspace")
            result.append(gis.record(workspace.root, p))
    return result


def source_layer(workspace, selection: dict) -> dict:
    collection = selection["source_collection_id"]
    source_id = selection["source_id"]
    path, entry = workspace.source_file(collection, source_id)
    native = Path(entry["body"].get("view_path", entry["body"]["filename"]))
    view = path
    for _ in native.parts:
        view = view.parent
    primary = gis.record(workspace.root, path)
    if primary["sha256"] != entry["body"]["sha256"] or primary["bytes"] != entry["body"]["bytes"]:
        raise ValueError("Original source view identity differs")
    companions = []
    for body in entry.get("companions", []):
        p = view / body.get("view_path", body["filename"])
        rec = gis.record(workspace.root, p)
        if rec["sha256"] != body["sha256"] or rec["bytes"] != body["bytes"]:
            raise ValueError("Original source companion identity differs")
        companions.append(rec)
    row = {"id": selection.get("id", "source:"+collection+":"+source_id),
           "title": selection.get("title", entry["title"]), "kind": entry["kind"],
           "file": primary, "companions": companions,
           "group": selection.get("group", "Original source layers"),
           "units": selection.get("units", entry.get("units", "source attributes")),
           "purpose": selection.get("purpose", entry.get("purpose") or ("categorical" if entry.get("role") == "NLCD" else "context")),
           "source": {"collection_id": collection, "id": source_id, "title": entry["title"],
                      "uri": entry["uri"], "vintage": entry["vintage"],
                      "sha256": entry["body"]["sha256"], "role": entry.get("role"),
                      "units": entry.get("units"), "conversion": entry.get("conversion"),
                      "received_gis":entry.get("received_gis")},
           "visible": selection.get("visible", False)}
    for key in ("layer", "where", "band", "metric", "direction"):
        if key in selection:
            row[key] = selection[key]
        elif key in ("layer", "metric", "direction") and entry.get(key) is not None:
            row[key] = entry[key]
    return row


def request(workspace, selection: dict) -> dict:
    """Select retained source editions, prepared grids and completed run artifacts.

    A source-only selection is fully usable before model execution. A selected run
    must be complete. No invented native-stage unit mappings are supplied here.
    """
    layers, attachments, grid_ids, run_ids = [], [], [], []
    source_selections = list(selection.get("sources", []))
    collection_id = selection.get("source_collection_id")
    if collection_id and not source_selections:
        source_selections = [{"source_collection_id": collection_id, "source_id": e["id"]}
                             for e in workspace._get("sources", collection_id)["entries"]]
    source_selections = [{**item, "source_collection_id": item.get("source_collection_id") or collection_id}
                         for item in source_selections]
    # Adopted working layers always retain their attached originals, licences and
    # edition provenance, including when the operator selected only GIS layers.
    selected_pairs={(x["source_collection_id"],x["source_id"]) for x in source_selections}
    for cid in dict.fromkeys(x["source_collection_id"] for x in source_selections):
        if not cid:continue
        collection=workspace._get("sources",cid)
        context_groups={e.get("gis_context_group") for e in collection["entries"]
                        if (cid,e["id"]) in selected_pairs and e.get("gis_context_group")}
        for entry in collection["entries"]:
            if entry.get("gis_required_context") and entry.get("gis_context_group") in context_groups and (cid,entry["id"]) not in selected_pairs:
                source_selections.append({"source_collection_id":cid,"source_id":entry["id"]})
                selected_pairs.add((cid,entry["id"]))
    for item in source_selections:
        if not item["source_collection_id"]:
            raise ValueError("Select the retained source collection for every source")
        row = source_layer(workspace, item)
        (layers if row["kind"] in {"vector", "raster"} else attachments).append(row)
    if selection.get("grid_id"):
        grid_ids.append(selection["grid_id"])
    if selection.get("baseline_run_id"):
        run_ids.append(selection["baseline_run_id"])
    run_ids.extend(selection.get("scenario_run_ids", []))
    if len(set(run_ids)) != len(run_ids):
        raise ValueError("Select each retained run once")
    runs = []
    for index, run_id in enumerate(run_ids):
        state = workspace.inspect_run(run_id)
        if state["state"] != "complete":
            raise ValueError("Finish the selected run before including its physical results: "+run_id)
        case = workspace._get("scenarios", state["selection"]["scenario_id"])
        profile = workspace._get("profiles", state["selection"]["profile_id"])
        run_directory = workspace.root / "runs" / run_id
        prefix = "Baseline" if index == 0 and selection.get("baseline_run_id") else "Case"
        for metric, item in state["artifacts"].items():
            if Path(item["path"]).suffix.lower() not in {".tif", ".tiff"}:
                continue
            if not item.get("units"):
                raise ValueError("Retained model artifact lacks declared physical units: "+metric)
            rec = _artifact(workspace, run_directory, item)
            layers.append({"id":"run:"+run_id+":"+metric,
                           "title":metric.replace("_", " ").capitalize()+" · "+case["title"],
                           "kind":"raster", "file":rec, "companions":_raster_companions(workspace, rec),
                           "group":prefix+" · "+case["title"]+" · "+run_id[:10],
                           "purpose":"physical", "metric":metric, "units":item["units"],
                           "run_id":run_id, "scenario_id":case["id"], "profile_id":profile["id"],
                           "visible":index == 0 and metric == "nitrogen_export",
                           "source":{"kind":"original completed model artifact", "artifact":item,
                                     "run_selection":state["selection"], "runtime":state.get("runtime", {}),
                                     "scenario":case, "profile":profile}})
        if "landcover" in state.get("stages", {}):
            item=state["stages"]["landcover"]["artifact"]
            rec=_artifact(workspace,run_directory,item)
            layers.append({"id":"scenario-landcover:"+run_id,"title":"Land cover · "+case["title"],
                           "kind":"raster","file":rec,"companions":_raster_companions(workspace,rec),
                           "group":prefix+" · "+case["title"]+" · "+run_id[:10],
                           "purpose":"categorical","units":item.get("units","class"),
                           "scenario_id":case["id"],"run_id":run_id,"visible":False})
        grid_ids.append(state["selection"]["grid_id"])
        runs.append({"id":run_id,"selection":state["selection"],"scenario_title":case["title"],
                     "profile_title":profile["title"],"runtime":state.get("runtime",{})})
    grids=[]
    for grid_id in dict.fromkeys(grid_ids):
        grid=workspace.get_grid(grid_id)
        grids.append(grid)
        if not selection.get("include_grid", True):
            continue
        directory=workspace.root/"grids"/grid_id
        for role,item in grid["files"].items():
            ext=Path(item["path"]).suffix.lower()
            if ext not in {".tif",".tiff",".gpkg"}:
                continue
            rec=_artifact(workspace,directory,item)
            kind="vector" if ext==".gpkg" else "raster"
            row={"id":"grid:"+grid_id+":"+role,"title":role.replace("_"," ").capitalize(),
                 "kind":kind,"file":rec,"group":"Prepared study grid · "+grid_id[:10],
                 "units":item.get("units","source geometry" if kind=="vector" else None),
                 "purpose":"categorical" if role in {"NLCD","reporting_mask"} else "context",
                 "source":{"kind":"original prepared grid","grid_id":grid_id,"role":role,
                           "input":grid.get("inputs",{}).get(role),"spec":grid["spec"]},
                 "visible":role=="reporting_area"}
            if kind=="raster":
                row["companions"]=_raster_companions(workspace,rec)
            else:
                row["layer"]=role
            layers.append(row)
    # Explicit existing comparison results: preserve their actual sign convention.
    for comparison_id in selection.get("comparison_ids", []):
        if not isinstance(comparison_id,str) or not __import__('re').fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}",comparison_id):
            raise ValueError("Select a retained comparison identity")
        directory=workspace.root/"comparisons"/comparison_id
        comparison=gis.load(directory/"comparison.json")
        if comparison["id"]!=comparison_id:
            raise ValueError("Comparison identity differs")
        for alternative in comparison["alternatives"]:
            for metric,item in alternative["artifacts"].items():
                rec=_artifact(workspace,directory,item)
                layers.append({"id":"comparison:"+comparison_id+":"+alternative["run_id"]+":"+metric,
                    "title":metric.replace("_"," ").capitalize()+" change · "+alternative["run_id"][:10],
                    "kind":"raster","file":rec,"companions":_raster_companions(workspace,rec),
                    "group":"Signed changes · "+comparison_id[:10],"purpose":"difference",
                    "metric":metric,"units":item["units"],"direction":comparison["direction"],
                    "run_id":alternative["run_id"],"profile_id":alternative["selection"]["profile_id"],
                    "scenario_id":alternative["selection"]["scenario_id"],"visible":False,
                    "source":{"comparison_id":comparison_id,"baseline_run_id":comparison["baseline_run_id"],
                              "profile_changed":alternative.get("profile_changed")}})
    if not layers:
        raise ValueError("Choose actual source layers, a prepared grid or completed runs")
    project_crs=selection.get("project_crs")
    if not project_crs and grids:
        # Read the real retained reference rather than assuming a grid-JSON spelling.
        import rasterio
        grid=grids[0]
        path=gis.checked(workspace.root/"grids"/grid["id"],grid["files"]["NLCD"])
        with rasterio.open(path) as src:
            project_crs=src.crs.to_string()
    if not project_crs:
        raise ValueError("Select the GIS project's display CRS for a source-only handover")
    focus=selection.get("focus_layer_id")
    if not focus:
        focus=next((l["id"] for l in layers if l["id"].endswith(":reporting_area")),None)
    if not any(l.get("visible") for l in layers):
        layers[0]["visible"]=True
    result={"schema":gis.REQUEST_SCHEMA,"title":selection.get("title",workspace.project["title"]+" · editable GIS"),
            "project_crs":project_crs,"layers":layers,"attachments":attachments,
            "provenance":{"project_id":workspace.project["id"],"project_title":workspace.project["title"],
                          "runs":runs,"grid_ids":list(dict.fromkeys(grid_ids)),
                          "source_collection_ids":list(dict.fromkeys(x["source_collection_id"] for x in source_selections)),
                          "notes":selection.get("notes",[])}}
    if focus:
        result["focus_layer_id"]=focus
    return result


def export(workspace, selection: dict, *, progress=None) -> dict:
    spec=request(workspace,selection)
    key=gis.fingerprint({"request":spec,"builder_version":gis.VERSION})
    folder=workspace.root/"gis-exports"/key
    folder.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    gis.save(folder/"selection.json",selection)
    result=gis.build(spec,workspace.root,folder/"project",progress=progress)
    archive=gis.pack(folder/"project",folder/"editable-gis.zip")
    value={"schema":"upstate.gis-export/v1","id":key,"state":"complete",
           "project_id":workspace.project["id"],"title":spec["title"],"result":result,
           "archive":gis.record(workspace.root,folder/"editable-gis.zip"),
           "open":(folder/"project"/"OPEN_GIS.html").relative_to(workspace.root).as_posix(),
           "project":(folder/"project"/"project.qgz").relative_to(workspace.root).as_posix()}
    gis.save(folder/"export.json",value)
    return value


def catalogue(workspace) -> dict:
    """Small, direct operator inventory; no complete source objects on every refresh."""
    sources=[]
    for collection in workspace.sources():
        sources.append({"id":collection["id"],"title":collection["title"],
                        "entries":[{k:e.get(k) for k in ("id","title","kind","role","units","gis_context_group","gis_required_context")}
                                   for e in collection["entries"]]})
    runs=[]
    for path in sorted((workspace.root/"runs").glob("*/run.json")):
        r=gis.load(path)
        runs.append({"id":r["id"],"state":r["state"],"selection":r["selection"],
                     "artifacts":[{"id":k,"units":v.get("units")} for k,v in r.get("artifacts",{}).items()]})
    exports=[gis.load(p) for p in sorted((workspace.root/"gis-exports").glob("*/export.json"))]
    return {"schema":"upstate.gis-catalogue/v1","project_id":workspace.project["id"],
            "sources":sources,"runs":runs,"exports":exports}


def received(workspace, receipt_id: str):
    """Read the original retained receiving record and its complete unchanged edition."""
    from .common import identifier
    parent=workspace.root/'gis-received'/identifier(receipt_id)
    value=gis.load(parent/'receipt.json')
    if value.get('id')!=receipt_id or value.get('project_id')!=workspace.project['id'] or value.get('state')!='complete':
        raise ValueError('Choose a complete GIS receiving from this scientific Workspace')
    result=gis.verify(parent/'project')
    if result['fingerprint']!=value['result']['fingerprint']:
        raise ValueError('Receive the newly sealed edition before adopting edited GIS files')
    return parent,value,result


def receive(workspace, archive: str | Path, *, source_upload_id: str | None=None) -> dict:
    """One receiving writer for the original Operator and the installed Workspace CLI."""
    import json
    import zipfile
    archive=Path(archive).resolve(strict=True)
    original=gis.record(archive.parent,archive)
    key=gis.fingerprint({'schema':'upstate.gis-receiving/v1','project_id':workspace.project['id'],
                         'archive_sha256':original['sha256']})
    parent=workspace.root/'gis-received'/key
    parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    root=parent/'project'
    with gis.locked(parent/'.receiving.lock'):
        if root.exists():
            result=gis.verify(root)
            with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as z:
                incoming=json.loads(z.read('inventory.json'))
            if incoming['fingerprint']!=result['fingerprint']:
                raise ValueError('The received directory differs from the supplied GIS edition')
        else:
            result=gis.receive(archive,root)
        target=parent/'editable-gis.zip'
        gis.copy_checked(archive.parent,original,target)
        value={'schema':'upstate.gis-receiving/v1','id':key,'state':'complete',
               'project_id':workspace.project['id'],'title':gis.load(root/'project.json')['title'],
               'result':result,'archive':gis.record(workspace.root,target),
               'source_archive_sha256':original['sha256']}
        receipt=parent/'receipt.json'
        if receipt.exists():
            prior=gis.load(receipt)
            if prior.get('source_archive_sha256')!=original['sha256']:
                raise ValueError('The existing receiving belongs to another archive')
            if prior.get('upload_id'):value['upload_id']=prior['upload_id']
        if source_upload_id and 'upload_id' not in value:value['upload_id']=source_upload_id
        gis.save(receipt,value)
        return value


def adopt_sources(workspace, selection: dict) -> dict:
    """Adopt selected received working layers through the ORIGINAL source importer.

    This appends an independent source edition; it does not edit any original
    source collection, grid, parameter profile, scenario, numerical run or receipt.
    """
    parent,receipt,result=received(workspace,selection['receipt_id'])
    root=parent/'project';project=gis.load(root/'project.json')
    reason=selection.get('reason','').strip()
    title=selection.get('title','').strip()
    if not reason or not title:
        raise ValueError('Name the new source edition and explain the adoption')
    chosen=selection.get('layer_ids')
    if not isinstance(chosen,list) or not chosen or len(set(chosen))!=len(chosen) or any(not isinstance(x,str) for x in chosen):
        raise ValueError('Choose each received working layer once')
    byid={l['id']:l for l in project['layers']}
    if set(chosen)-set(byid):raise ValueError('Choose existing received layer identities')
    adopted={'schema':'upstate.gis-source-adoption-selection/v1','adopter_version':gis.VERSION,
             'project_id':workspace.project['id'],'receipt_id':receipt['id'],
             'received_edition_id':project['edition_id'],'fingerprint':result['fingerprint'],
             'title':title,'reason':reason,'layer_ids':chosen}
    key=gis.fingerprint(adopted)
    directory=workspace.root/'gis-source-adoptions'/key
    directory.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    with gis.locked(directory/'.adoption.lock'):
        state=directory/'adoption.json'
        if state.exists():
            prior=gis.load(state)
            if prior['selection']!=adopted:raise ValueError('Source adoption selection changed')
            collection=workspace._get('sources',prior['source_collection_id'])
            for entry in collection['entries']:workspace.source_file(collection['id'],entry['id'])
            return prior
        # Keep source paths relative to the existing receipt parent. Original
        # Workspace.import_sources performs its normal complete object retention.
        entries=[]
        for layer_id in chosen:
            row=byid[layer_id];path=gis.local(root,row['working_path'])
            data=row['data'];companions=[]
            if data['kind']=='raster':
                import rasterio
                with rasterio.open(path) as src:
                    for filename in src.files:
                        p=Path(filename).resolve(strict=True)
                        if p==path:continue
                        rec=gis.record(root,gis.local(root,p.relative_to(root).as_posix()))
                        companions.append({'path':'project/'+rec['path'],'sha256':rec['sha256']})
            entry={'id':'GIS_'+row['key'],'title':row['title'],'kind':data['kind'],
                   'path':'project/'+row['working_path'],'sha256':gis.sha256(path),'companions':companions,
                   'gis_context_group':key,
                   'uri':'urn:upstate:received-gis:'+receipt['id']+':'+row['key'],
                   'vintage':'Received GIS edition '+project['edition_id'],'units':data['units'],
                   'received_gis':{'receipt_id':receipt['id'],'edition_id':project['edition_id'],
                                   'layer_id':row['id'],'originals':row['originals'],
                                   'source':row.get('source'),'run_id':row.get('run_id'),
                                   'scenario_id':row.get('scenario_id'),'profile_id':row.get('profile_id'),
                                   'purpose':row.get('purpose'),'metric':row.get('metric'),
                                   'direction':row.get('direction'),'adoption_id':key,'reason':reason}}
            for name in ('purpose','metric','direction'):
                if row.get(name) is not None:entry[name]=row[name]
            original_source=row.get('source') or {}
            for name in ('role','conversion'):
                if original_source.get(name) is not None:entry[name]=original_source[name]
            if data['kind']=='vector':entry['layer']=data['layer']
            entries.append(entry)
        seen_context=set()
        def context(title, records):
            signature=tuple((r['path'],r['sha256']) for r in records)
            if signature in seen_context:return
            seen_context.add(signature)
            for rec in records:gis.checked(root,rec)
            code=gis.fingerprint(signature)
            entries.append({'id':'GIS_CONTEXT_'+code,'title':title,'kind':'document',
                            'path':'project/'+records[0]['path'],'sha256':records[0]['sha256'],
                            'companions':[{'path':'project/'+r['path'],'sha256':r['sha256']} for r in records[1:]],
                            'uri':'urn:upstate:received-gis:'+receipt['id']+':context:'+code,
                            'vintage':'Received GIS edition '+project['edition_id'],
                            'gis_context_group':key,'gis_required_context':True})
        for layer_id in chosen:
            context('Retained originals · '+byid[layer_id]['title'],byid[layer_id]['originals'])
        for document in project.get('attachments',[]):
            context(document['title'],document['files'])
        history=[gis.record(root,p) for p in sorted((root/'history').rglob('*')) if p.is_file()]
        context('Received GIS edition provenance and retained history',
                [gis.record(root,root/'project.json'),*history])
        manifest={'schema':'upstate.sources/v1','title':title,'entries':entries,
                  'notes':[reason,'Selected independently editable working layers adopted from a complete received GIS edition.'],
                  'scope':{'gis_source_adoption':adopted}}
        manifest_path=parent/('source-adoption-'+key+'.json')
        if manifest_path.exists() and gis.load(manifest_path)!=manifest:
            raise ValueError('The retained adoption manifest changed')
        gis.save(manifest_path,manifest)
        collection=workspace.import_sources(manifest_path)
        value={'schema':'upstate.gis-source-adoption/v1','id':key,'state':'complete',
               'project_id':workspace.project['id'],'selection':adopted,
               'source_collection_id':collection['id'],'title':title,
               'sources':[{'layer_id':layer_id,'source_id':'GIS_'+byid[layer_id]['key']}
                          for layer_id in chosen],
               'manifest':gis.record(workspace.root,manifest_path)}
        gis.save(state,value)
        return value

import argparse
import json

from .common import atomic_json, digest, read_json
from .workspace import Workspace
from . import parcel_source_desk as desk


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--workspace")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = commands.add_parser("capture", help="Inspect an existing original parcel capture")
    p.add_argument("directory")
    p.add_argument("--output")
    p = commands.add_parser("prepare", help="Prepare and import the selected original county edition")
    p.add_argument("directory")
    p.add_argument("--selection", required=True, help="Saved capture preview JSON")
    p.add_argument("--title", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--operation-id")
    commands.add_parser("overview")
    p = commands.add_parser("edition")
    p.add_argument("edition_id")
    p = commands.add_parser("rows")
    p.add_argument("edition_id")
    p.add_argument("--table", default="parcels", choices=list(desk.TABLES))
    p.add_argument("--county", default="")
    p.add_argument("--query", default="")
    p.add_argument("--offset", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=100)
    p = commands.add_parser("study-selection")
    p.add_argument("edition_id")
    p.add_argument("settings")
    p.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "capture":
        result = desk.preview(args.directory)
        if args.output:
            atomic_json(Path(args.output), result, immutable=True)
    else:
        if not args.workspace:
            parser.error("This operation needs --workspace for the existing original project")
        ws = Workspace(args.workspace)
        if args.command == "prepare":
            saved = read_json(args.selection)
            selection = saved.get("selection", saved)
            operation_id = args.operation_id or digest({
                "action": "parcel.source.prepare", "project_id": ws.project["id"],
                "selection": selection, "title": args.title,
            })
            result = desk.operate(ws, args.directory, selection, title=args.title, operation_id=operation_id)
        elif args.command == "overview":
            result = desk.overview(ws)
        elif args.command == "edition":
            result = desk.get(ws, args.edition_id)
        elif args.command == "rows":
            result = desk.rows(ws, args.edition_id, table=args.table, county=args.county,
                               query=args.query, offset=args.offset, limit=args.limit)
        else:
            result = desk.study_selection(ws, args.edition_id, read_json(args.settings))
            atomic_json(Path(args.output), result, immutable=True)
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Water and Habitat Context

Authored by TokenJunkieLabs.

This additive desk turns retained source editions into a saved, inspectable description of a selected reporting area. It covers mapped aquatic habitat, wetland inventory coverage, mapped hydrography, PAD-US inventory, authoritative stream order, and spatial relationships to supplied HUC or utility boundaries.

The calculation uses the existing scientific Workspace. It reads original retained vector bodies through the application's Fiona/GDAL environment and supports prepared NWI_CONTEXT rasters through their original class dictionary and mapping-status companion.

## Integration

Place these two complete files alongside the current application:

- model/water_context.py
- model/WATER_CONTEXT.md

The public interface is:

    from model import water_context
    catalog = water_context.catalog(workspace)
    record = water_context.build(workspace, spec)
    records = water_context.list_saved(workspace)
    reopened = water_context.get_saved(workspace, record["id"])
    map_data = water_context.preview(workspace, record["id"])
    verification = water_context.verify_all(workspace)

Each function accepts an existing Workspace instance or its root directory. GIS imports and original source verification occur during an explicit build. Catalog, list and get calls read retained JSON metadata. Preview reads its precomputed display artifact. The existing operator queue should invoke build; the source module creates no server, queue or model engine.

The core composes with the existing APIs:

- Workspace.sources(), _get("sources", collection_id), source_file(collection_id, source_id).
- Workspace._save("water-context-selections", spec), which returns a content-addressed immutable selection.
- model.rasters.native_vector_path and vector_environment, including original gzip carriers.
- model.common atomic_json, atomic_bytes, digest, identifier, describe_file, verify_file, relative_file and held.

## Selection specification

    {
      "title": "Upper Savannah water and habitat context",
      "boundary": {
        "collection_id": "<retained source collection hash>",
        "source_id": "<retained reporting/HUC/utility polygon source>",
        "layer": "<optional native layer>",
        "where": {"HUC12": "<optional exact native value>"},
        "id_field": "<optional native feature ID field>",
        "feature_ids": ["<optional selected native IDs>"]
      },
      "overlays": {
        "wetlands": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NWI source>"},
        "mapping_status": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NWI mapping status>"},
        "flowlines": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NHD flowline source>"},
        "waterbodies": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NHD waterbody source>"},
        "protected_lands": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<PAD-US manager inventory>"},
        "stream_order": {"collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<NHD_STREAM_ORDER source>"}
      },
      "measurement_crs": "EPSG:5070",
      "relations": [
        {"kind": "huc", "collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<HUC polygons>"},
        {"kind": "utility", "collection_id": "<hash>", "source_id": "<utility polygons>"}
      ]
    }

All overlays and relationship sources are optional. A polygon selection is required. References accept the same layer, equality filter, native ID field and explicit ID selection as the primary boundary. NWI mapping status uses all retained status records; its where and feature_ids filters are rejected so Digital, No_Data and unknown records participate in the same partition. Select its geographic extent through the reporting boundary. Equality filters use actual native values and field names; they do not become SQL expressions. Multiple selected reporting features are dissolved for the headline denominator.

The two NHD roles remain separately selectable even when both original entries declare role NHD. The optional stream_order selector uses an independently supplied NHD_STREAM_ORDER source and its native streamorde/streamorder field. It carries native NHDPlusID and permanent_identifier values into the tables and retains all original properties. Source capture and flow routing remain with their existing components.

If wetlands selects a prepared NWI_CONTEXT raster and mapping_status is omitted, the core uses its declared mapping_status_path companion. The paired companion must be present in that exact retained source entry. The final normalized selection records this choice.

## Result and saved files

## Metric fields

Every category returns status, label, feature_count, footprint_count, area_ha, length_km, area_pct, coverage_pct and classes. Unavailable inputs use status unavailable and null metrics. A loaded empty inventory supplies zero observed inventory with its source edition still listed. Raster-derived footprint counts are distinguished from native feature counts; feature_count is null for a raster source.

NWI inventory, NHD waterbody and PAD-US headline areas are geometric unions clipped to the selected boundary. NHD mapped flowline and authoritative stream-order lengths use unions of coincident linework. Repeated coincident geometry therefore does not inflate totals.

Native classes retain their values and source field names. NWI uses WETLAND_TYPE; NHD uses ftype; PAD-US uses GAP_Sts and separately exposes manager_classes when Mang_Type/Man_Type exists; stream order uses the authoritative streamorde field. Field lookup accepts case and layer-name qualification while exported properties preserve their original names.

Class areas can overlap one another. Individual native features may appear in several boundary relationships. Per-class, per-HUC and per-utility values should be read independently; the headline total always uses the union of the selected reporting boundary and the relevant inventory.

Each per-boundary summary also retains source_boundary_area_ha, selected_overlap_area_ha, selection_share_pct and source_boundary_share_pct. selection_share_pct divides the selected overlap by the union of the reporting selection. source_boundary_share_pct divides the same overlap by the full original native polygon area. Local inventory percentages use only the selected overlap.

### NWI status partition

Let D be the union of native STATUS Digital polygons, N the union of No_Data polygons, U the union of unrecognized-status polygons, and B the selected boundary.

- Digital-only coverage is D minus N and U.
- Provider No_Data-only coverage is N minus D and U.
- Conflicting coverage is the intersection of D and N, minus U.
- Unknown coverage is B minus the preceding three disjoint regions.

The result provides covered_area_ha, unmapped_area_ha, digital_area_ha, provider_no_data_area_ha, conflicting_area_ha, unknown_area_ha, partition_total_area_ha and unknown_native_status_values. covered_area_ha and digital_area_ha both describe Digital-only coverage. coverage_pct is that area divided by the selected boundary. unmapped_area_ha is the remainder of the selected boundary, including unknown and conflicting coverage.

The wetland inventory summary also provides mapped_occurrence_area_ha, mapped_no_selected_occurrence_area_ha, and published_occurrence_outside_mapped_area_ha when both inventories are selected. The no-selected-occurrence field refers to the selected retained source and any category/feature filters. The compatibility alias mapped_no_published_occurrence_area_ha is populated only for an unfiltered selected inventory and remains qualified to that source edition and acquisition scope. A positive published NWI polygon remains visible where the separately dated status is No_Data, conflicting or unknown.

NWI includes mapped aquatic habitat such as ponds, lakes, riverine and deepwater classes. Its total area is labelled NWI mapped aquatic habitat inventory. A Digital area without a published polygon describes the selected inventory edition; field-confirmed absence requires separate observation.

### Prepared NWI_CONTEXT grids

The reader uses the entry's top-level codes, mapping_status_codes and mapping_status_path, with metadata-wrapped equivalents supported. The native source grid remains unchanged.

Occurrence code 0 represents Digital mapping with no published NWI polygon. Codes 1 through 252 retain their supplied class dictionary; 254 retains its explicit overlapping-type meaning; 255 supplies no occurrence value. Positive occurrence is independent of the mapping-status raster.

Mapping-status codes are 0 unknown, 1 Digital, 2 No_Data, 3 conflicting Digital and No_Data, and 255 outside the selected original domain. Status 255 contributes to unknown coverage if a new reporting selection extends outside that domain.

The reader uses blockwise rasterio.features.shapes, then exact intersection of the original cell footprints with the selected boundary. Raster hectares describe clipped grid-cell footprints. They can differ from pixel-centre summaries or original vector-polygon areas. No per-cell Shapely object is created for every grid cell, and no raster resampling is performed.

### Hydrography and PAD-US

Mapped flowline length includes the selected native ftype inventory, including ArtificialPath or Connector where present. The explicit native class breakdown identifies that content.

PAD-US inventory overlap preserves manager, owner, GAP status, source date and native identifiers as supplied. Manager identity alone does not determine conservation status. GAP values remain original strings, and absent classification fields remain absent. The headline is unique inventory overlap.

Utility/source-water polygons keep their supplied labels and footprint meaning. A surface-water protection buffer is represented as that source's spatial footprint. Intersections describe spatial relationships; they do not establish upstream routing, stream order, habitat condition or pollutant retention.

## Projection, geometry and map display

The default area CRS is EPSG:5070, NAD83 / Conus Albers. Configurable measurement CRSs must be projected with horizontal metre units. The operator is responsible for selecting an appropriate projected area CRS for another geography. Area uses the full projected geometry; horizontal line length uses WGS84 ellipsoidal geodesic measurement after clipping.

The vector reader uses the original Fiona/GDAL helpers. The accepted overlay collector already retains original true-curve responses and their provider-generated linear analytical representation with matching native IDs. Source Z/M and original curve evidence remain in the retained source edition. The analytical geometry uses XY.

Any required topological make_valid operation is written to geometry-corrections.json with source/feature identity and before/after WKB hashes. Original source bodies remain intact.

features.geojson contains all selected derived geometries in WGS84 longitude/latitude. Preview uses a round-robin sample of at most 2,500 display features and 30-metre topology-preserving simplification. Its truncation and simplification are explicit. Neither changes the quantitative calculation or complete export.

## Prepare the original scientific inputs

The workspace needs completed native baseline runs and an admitted annual-load observation edition. Each candidate group contains runs from the same original grid and unchanged land-cover baseline. The candidate table shows each run's actual NDR/SDR models and available pollutants alongside its retained parameter profile. A profile may have separately completed partial and combined runs; each retains its original native run identity. Select the original catchment polygon source and ID field used by the observations.

The native catalog exposes compatible runs and the retained observations. A useful selection needs comparable observed annual loads for at least one of nitrogen, phosphorus or sediment. Native nitrogen and phosphorus loads retain kilograms per year; sediment retains metric tonnes per year. The original observation pipeline retains accepted rows, contextual rows, qualifiers, source references and units.

The source edition and catchments must belong to the same scientific workspace. The calibration inspector reads the actual polygon layer. It connects overlapping upstream catchments and repeated station identifiers into whole spatial groups, then retains the source geometry and native references used to derive those groups.

## Select profiles and annual observations

The objective controls follow the original annual observations and the pollutants shared by the selected completed runs. Unsupported pollutants have zero weight. An NDR-only comparison can therefore calibrate nitrogen and phosphorus while an original mixed observation edition keeps its sediment rows and native exclusions. When an output becomes available again, the form restores the weight entered for it. The saved objective remains explicit.

1. Open **Calibration and validation** and choose **New calibration**.
2. Give the selection a study title. Choose the retained grid and baseline, then check the completed candidate runs. Inspect the actual model outputs beside each profile; NDR-only, SDR-only and combined runs stay distinguishable.
3. Choose the original annual-load observation edition. **Inspect original observations** opens its original records and downloads.
4. Choose the catchment source edition and polygon source. Use **Inspect native source fields** to see the actual layer names, field types, feature count and first original features. Select the catchment ID field that matches the observations.
5. If needed, add exact field filters with their real data types. The optional observation record list selects actual retained record IDs, one per line.
6. Choose observation-period weighting. **Complete years** gives complete annual periods equal weight, including leap years. **Elapsed days** uses the original covered duration for documented annualized period rates. Keep this choice consistent with the original annual-estimation method.
7. Set the relative pollutant weights. A zero weight excludes that pollutant from parameter selection. Automatic normalization uses calibration observations only. A study-specific normalization scale must be positive and must include its source or rationale.
8. Choose **Inspect original catchments**. After the original source inspection completes, assign entire groups to calibration or validation. Keep at least one group for calibration. Giving two groups the same name merges them; merged groups must share the same role.
9. Choose **Save calibration selection**. The existing operator task queue retains an immutable calibration plan.

The form retains its draft for the selected workspace in the current browser session, including temporarily invalid entries. Changing source inputs invalidates the previous catchment preview, so the next save inspects the corresponding original source selection. Revising a saved plan creates a new immutable selection.

The advanced panel supports an explicit reference candidate for exact score ties and a delivered external annual load linked to an actual original observation record. Each delivered load requires its annual mass, units and original source reference. The native science module validates this additional contribution before using it with the diffuse-load prediction. Use the observation/source notes to retain reservoir, point-source and annual-period context.

## Analyze and inspect the results

Open a saved selection and choose **Analyze selection**. The single existing operator worker evaluates retained completed native runs. The science module reuses matching original observation comparisons, persists completed candidate work, and resumes from that progress after an interruption.

The analysis ranks eligible profiles using the saved calibration groups, pollutant weights and normalization. Group weighting keeps a repeated station or a dense cluster of related upstream catchments from silently becoming independent replicated evidence. Reserved validation groups assess the selected profile after selection. If the plan reserves no validation groups, the saved evaluation design is calibration only.

Open **Results** from the completed task or saved selection. The interface includes:

| View | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Profile ranking | Calibration objective, selected candidate, actual NDR/SDR outputs, completed native run links and retained candidate outcomes. |
| Physical fit | Per-pollutant calibration errors, physical units, catchment/group counts and normalized mean squared error. |
| Independent validation | Selected-profile performance on the reserved spatial groups. |
| Observed and modeled | Each selected-profile catchment/pollutant prediction beside its original annual reference, period and source record IDs. |
| Catchment groups | The retained calibration/validation assignments, original catchments, stations and admitted record counts. |
| Candidate envelope | Annual-load ranges across the calibration Pareto candidates, with original candidate-run counts, distinct-profile counts and expected profiles. |
| Group stability | Selection after leaving out each calibration group, including whether the chosen run and profile remain unchanged, using retained native predictions and normalization from the remaining calibration groups. |
| Exclusions | Original reference exclusions, incomplete native support and candidate-specific errors retained by the scientific analysis. |

The observed-versus-modeled charts keep pollutants separate and use their physical units. Filled circles show calibration catchments; outlined squares show validation catchments. The dashed line marks equality. Every chart point comes from the selected candidate's retained, included prediction rows.

Search, sort and page the result tables to find a profile, catchment, pollutant or source record. Every original row remains in the downloaded CSV and complete JSON records. The **Original complete analysis record** contains the full methods, source vintages, normalization, validation support and candidate outcomes.

A candidate requires the complete declared calibration support before it can enter the ranking. An analysis with no eligible candidate retains an explicit result and reports the native support problem in the operator task. Open the saved selection to inspect that retained result, address the source or native-run outcome, and rerun or revise the selection.

### Interpret the scientific comparisons

A lower normalized calibration objective identifies the selected retained profile. Physical RMSE, mean bias and other pollutant metrics describe its errors in the original annual mass units. Normalization is derived from the calibration references, or from the study-specific scale saved with its rationale.

A reserved spatial split separates parameter selection from the selected-profile validation report. It does not create a new observed time series or add independent years to an annual model. The original period assumptions remain attached to the records.

The candidate envelope describes the calibration Pareto set: candidates whose pollutant scores are not jointly dominated by another candidate. Its range reflects the retained candidate runs and their coverage. A single profile can have separate NDR, SDR or combined run variants, so the result shows both run counts and distinct-profile counts. The median and range retain the original candidate-run weighting recorded in the scientific report. Original run IDs remain available for every comparison.

Leaving one calibration group out evaluates the stability of the selection among the original completed candidates. It uses their retained predictions, with the held calibration group removed from that fold's normalization and selection. Separately reserved validation groups stay outside those folds.

```javascript
  temporal_weighting: binding.recommended_temporal_weighting,
  title: 'Annual-load calibration',
  workspace_key: state.workspace_key,

```

The optional `workspace_key` guards the selected operator workspace; it is the original operator key, not the internal project UUID. The method verifies that the actual observation edition is admitted in the current catalog and that the selected catchment source is a retained vector entry. The source desk refreshes the ordinary workspace state after its bind task completes, so that new source entry is available.

This opens the normal calibration form with the original observation and catchment identities. It preserves the workspace draft's selected native grid, baseline, candidate run IDs, objective weights, title, notes and catchment-group choices. A new observation edition clears record filters and delivered external loads tied to the preceding observation IDs. Catchment filters come from the new binding. The normal preview resolves the actual spatial groups before a plan is saved.

An explicit saved period-weighting choice remains the user's choice. Otherwise, the form initializes from the supplied binding's weighting or the selected observation metadata's `recommended_temporal_weighting`. Changing observations follows their actual recommendation until the user edits the period control. Saved plans and drafts from earlier editions keep their original weighting.

The binding remains in the workspace draft even if no completed native baseline candidate exists yet. After a baseline finishes, **New calibration** reopens that original observation and catchment selection. Newer form requests supersede earlier pending catalog reads, candidate checkboxes restore by original run ID, and a previous task response leaves a subsequently opened draft intact.

## Operator API

The descriptor registers these routes with the existing authenticated local operator and selected workspace. Its state contribution is `state.data.calibration`, containing `calibration_plans` and `calibrations`. The original `/api/item` route also accepts the registered kinds `calibration-plans` and `calibrations`.

| Method | Route | Selection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/calibration/catalog?workspace=...` | Compatible completed run groups and admitted original observation editions. |
| POST | `/api/calibration/preview` | JSON body with `workspace` and native `selection`; reads original catchments and derives groups. |
| GET | `/api/calibration/plan?workspace=...&id=...` | Retained plan, persisted progress and original JSON download. |

The original-source preview takes the workspace's existing native-operation gate. The interface can continue displaying retained reports while the worker completes a scientific operation. Source inspection during active native work returns the existing busy response and leaves the form draft available.

`operator/calibration.py` adapts the scientific records and writes comparison exports. `operator/web/calibration.mjs` provides the existing operator's calibration view and forms. `operator/web/calibration.css` supplies scoped monochrome styling. `operator/extensions/calibration.json` binds them to the maintained extension host. `operator/install_calibration.py` performs current-source registration and migration; `source_tools/calibration_assembly.py` composes the complete receiving edition before its final source identities are recorded.

The scientific model API remains `catalog(workspace)`, `preview(workspace, selection)`, `prepare(workspace, selection)`, `inspect(workspace, plan_id)`, and `analyze(workspace, plan_id)`. See the companion model guide for the complete scientific input schema and source-native command-line workflow.

## Published observation-error sensitivity

Open a completed nominal calibration and select **Analyze published observation errors**. The existing task queue reuses its original modeled predictions, selected candidate, catchment groups, pollutant weights and normalization scales. Choose a finite nonnegative standard-error multiplier. The default is **1**; **0** reproduces the nominal comparison.

The source is the standard error retained with each original annual observation. The scientific module retains conversion to annual comparison units and the temporal aggregation already used by the nominal calibration. Missing standard errors remain explicit in source coverage and affected comparison rows. No default percentage or replacement error is supplied.

The completed analysis appears in **Published observation uncertainty** on the original calibration page. Open it to inspect:

- **Ranking sensitivity:** each challenger's nominal, minimum and maximum objective gap relative to the originally selected run. A positive gap favors the original selection. The plot marks zero, the source-error range and the nominal gap; the complete table remains searchable and sortable.
- **First-tie multiplier:** the earliest standard-error multiplier that can produce a tie under the fixed objective and nonnegative source bounds. Missing contributing errors, equivalent predictions and thresholds outside finite numerical representation retain their exact scientific state.
- **Annual reference ranges:** original catchment, hydrologic group, pollutant, annual mass, source record IDs and complete or incomplete uncertainty coverage.
- **Published standard errors:** original source values and units, converted annual standard errors and each retained source issue.
- **Source contributions:** coefficients and endpoints for original records contributing to each challenger comparison. A shared original record ID retains one source perturbation across all references that use it.
- **Selected validation:** modeled annual load and residual ranges for the originally selected model on reserved validation catchments, with native/source coverage retained. No challenger ranking uses these rows.
- **Nominal reproduction:** original and reproduced calibration objective values, absolute differences and numerical tolerance.

These are deterministic sensitivity ranges over the declared marginal source bounds. They do not assign a probability to a possible reversal or change the nominal selected profile. Dependence among distinct original estimates is not assumed away. Validation catchments remain outside challenger ranking; their reference bands and selected-model residual ranges are descriptive. Overall partial coverage can coexist with an exact comparison when the missing record's shared coefficient cancels, or at multiplier zero.

## Original-catchment residual maps

A completed calibration now opens its original catchment geometry as a retained
map source, grayscale atlas and editable GIS project. The same Calibration desk
owns the selection, queue, saved result and reopening. The source-error page can
also create a map edition using its exact retained standard-error multiplier and
missing-error coverage.

### Operate the complete map workflow

1. Open a completed nominal calibration and choose **Prepare residual maps**.
   From an observation sensitivity result choose **Map these reference ranges**
   to preselect that retained sensitivity edition.
2. Keep the original selected run. Optionally include eligible challenger runs
   from the same saved calibration. The selected run includes calibration and
   held-out descriptive rows; challenger layers contain calibration rows only.
   The form identifies each original native candidate and its calibration loss.
3. Submit **Prepare maps** through the existing workspace task queue. This calls
   the maintained `model.calibration_maps.prepare` and retains the source collection,
   map edition, CSV tables, SVG pages, PDF atlas and original scientific records.
   The completed task exposes those verified file downloads immediately.
4. Return to the same calibration. Its **Catchment residual maps** section lists
   every retained map edition. Open one, filter the layer list by candidate or
   pollutant, and choose **Atlas and files**. The page shows calibration/held-out
   row counts, incomplete native rows, units and the shared per-pollutant residual
   display cap. PDF opens its exact verified file ticket in the existing detail viewer; SVG pages appear directly
   and remain downloadable.
5. **Open source map** uses the original spatial viewer's `spatial-item` action
   with kind `source-info`, exact source collection and source ID. That viewer
   supplies boundaries and original scalar attribute inspection.
6. **Save original spatial review** queues the science module's original
   `SpatialReview.save` join. Calibration overlays are solid; held-out overlays
   are dashed. The immutable `calibration-map-reviews` link retains map, layer and
   original spatial review IDs. The saved-review button appears after the normal
   task/state refresh and reopens the existing spatial desk.
7. **Build editable GIS project** sends the map's exact `gis_selection` directly
   to the maintained `gis.project.export` action. The selected vector sources and
   their required context preserve GeoJSON, CSV, atlas pages and original source
   records in the ordinary GIS project. The existing completed task and
   **Editable GIS projects** view expose its ZIP, QGIS project and offline viewer.
8. Back up and reopen the original workspace. Existing recursive workspace and
   application collection includes `calibration-maps`, `calibration-map-reviews`,
   `calibration-map-exports`, the ordinary source objects and original spatial
   reviews. The extension receiving hook reopens each map through the science
   validator and validates linked reviews through `SpatialReview.validate_saved`.

### Scientific map meaning

A residual is the saved predicted annual load minus the time-weighted original
annual reference. Native modeled load and any explicitly retained delivered
external load remain separate attributes. Pollutant mass units, temporal/source
identities, native support and the calibration/held-out role travel with each
catchment. Incomplete native support stays null.

The atlas uses one absolute-residual display cap per pollutant across the chosen
candidate maps. Each panel retains an original catchment, including holes and
disconnected parts, in the actual saved model-grid CRS. GeoJSON uses EPSG:4326.
Nested or overlapping upstream catchments stay separate; their loads and
residuals are not summed into regional totals. The ordinary spatial source view
shows outline geometry and scalar attributes; the PDF/SVG atlas carries the
signed grayscale residual rendering.

When a source-error analysis is selected, the map retains that exact analysis's
reference bounds and missing-error state. It does not perform another native run,
change the original nominal profile or rank challengers using held-out values.

### Current implementation contract

The extension adds these original queue actions:

- `calibration.maps.prepare`: `{report_id, candidate_run_ids?, uncertainty_id?}`.
  Omitted candidate IDs select only the nominal run. Every explicit selection
  must include that run; all candidates must belong to the retained report.
- `calibration.maps.review`: `{map_id, layer_id}`.

`GET /api/calibration/maps?id=MAP_ID` returns `{workspace_key, map, reviews,
artifacts, _downloads}`. Every `artifacts` entry contains the exact original
relative file descriptor and its verified operator download ticket. Collection
item kind `calibration-maps` uses that same read operation. State includes compact
`calibration_maps` summaries and immutable `calibration_map_reviews` links.

The separate browser source `operator/web/calibration_maps.mjs` is imported by
the existing calibration module and declared in its maintained extension assets.
It owns map view state and narrow controls; the current shared app, spatial
viewer and GIS provider remain their own implementations. Workspace/request
guards discard stale map reads and form submissions. Source and review buttons
use the original app's native action contract.

Receive the complete science files `model/calibration_maps.py` and
`model/CALIBRATION_MAPS.md` with all eight operator/cohort files, then run the
same `operator/install_calibration.py --application ACTUAL_APP --source COHORT`.
The installer knows the exact merged PR2850 predecessors and still rejects
unrecognized competing edits. The cumulative assembly driver includes the new
module and browser asset while treating `model/spatial.py` as a shared native
dependency.

Native preparation needs the application's existing Fiona, Shapely, PyProj and
Matplotlib environment. The maintained original SpatialReview and Editable GIS
1.2.1 providers supply the review and GIS joins. Installed source should include
the current `operator/extensions/gis-projects.json`; no new GIS exporter or
shared-host fork is introduced. Scientific dependency and map-method details are
in [CALIBRATION_MAPS.md](../model/CALIBRATION_MAPS.md).

A focused native receiving check can compile `model/calibration_maps.py` and
`operator/calibration.py`, import the original provider, then prepare one actual
completed calibration's map edition, open its first PDF/SVG and scalar source,
save a review, export its GIS project and reopen the same workspace. Use actual
retained report IDs from that study.

def sha(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest()


def run(application, source_root, *, dry_run=False):
    application = Path(application).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
    source_root = Path(source_root).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
    missing = [name for name in DEPENDENCIES if not (application / name).is_file()]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError("Compose the current full application and original parcel engine first: " + ", ".join(missing))
    server = (application / "operator/server.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    browser = (application / "operator/web/app.mjs").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if "ExtensionRegistry" not in server or "extensions.render(" not in browser:
        raise ValueError("Apply the current original ECSA host installer to this application first")
    native = ast.parse((application / "source_tools/reporting_parcels.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    method = next((node.value.value for node in native.body
                   if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant)
                   and any(isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == "PREPARATION_METHOD"
                           for target in node.targets)), None)
    if not isinstance(method, str) or not method.startswith("upstate.reporting-parcels/whole-original-polygons/"):
        raise ValueError("Compose the current whole-original parcel preparation source before installing this desk")
    lock_root = application / ".locks"
    lock_root.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with (lock_root / "parcel-source-install.lock").open("a+") as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        pending, original = {}, {}
        for name in FILES:
            source = (source_root / name).resolve(strict=True)
            if not source.is_relative_to(source_root) or not source.is_file():
                raise ValueError("Receive the complete parcel desk source file: " + name)
            data = source.read_bytes()
            if name.endswith(".py"):
                ast.parse(data.decode("utf-8"), filename=name)
            if name.endswith(".json"):
                value = json.loads(data)
                if value.get("schema") != "upstate.operator-extension/v1" or value.get("id") != "parcel-sources":
                    raise ValueError("Receive the authored parcel-sources registration")
            target = application / name
            if target.is_symlink() or not target.parent.resolve().is_relative_to(application):
                raise ValueError("The installed source path must remain within the original application: " + name)
            before = target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None
            if before is not None and before != data:
                if name.endswith(".json") and json.loads(before) == json.loads(data):
                    data = before
                elif sha(before) not in (PREVIOUS[name], *PREVIOUS_EDITIONS.get(name, ())):
                    raise ValueError("Compose the current authored parcel desk before replacing " + name)
            original[name], pending[name] = before, data
        changed = [name for name in FILES if original[name] != pending[name]]
        result = {
            "schema": "upstate.parcel-source-install/v1", "application": str(application),
            "dry_run": dry_run, "changed": changed, "entrypoint": "/#parcel-sources",
            "preparation_method": method, "extension_id": "parcel-sources",
            "files": [{"path": name, "bytes": len(pending[name]), "sha256": sha(pending[name]),
                       "previous_sha256": sha(original[name]) if original[name] is not None else None}
                      for name in FILES],
        }
        if dry_run:
            return result
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".parcel-source-install-", dir=application.parent) as temporary:
            staging = Path(temporary)
            for name in changed:
                target = staging / name
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                target.write_bytes(pending[name])
            for name in changed:
                target = application / name
                before = target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None
                if before != original[name]:
                    raise RuntimeError("The current source changed during composition: " + name)
            for name in changed:
                target = application / name
                before = target.read_bytes() if target.exists() else None
                if before != original[name]:
                    raise RuntimeError("The current source changed during composition: " + name)
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                os.replace(staging / name, target)
        return result


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--application", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--source-root", default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    print(json.dumps(run(args.application, args.source_root, dry_run=args.dry_run), indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
